title: CPU-gate rework, part 2: the backstop's VEX/EVEX and POPCNT classifier, the crash handler's #UD takeover (with the cpu_gate annotation), and check 5's ud2/EVEX backstop fixtures before and after crash-handler install
acceptance: 09 §2.1 WP-0.5r row (Director branch docs/plan/09-roadmap-and-process.md:103, identical on main), acceptance criterion CL-17 (early), the part that is still open after #65: "A `ud2` trap and an EVEX fault after crash-handler install both produce a minidump, never the CPU message." On Linux the Phase 0 crash handler writes a text report (crash.h), so the dump there is the .txt report.

Same row, scope clause (round-5 backstop rules): "the illegal-instruction backstop keeps its trap passthrough (`ud2`/`ud1`/`ud0`, already in both hooks) and adds the VEX/EVEX and POPCNT classifier, so only a genuine ISA fault gets the CPU message; the crash handler takes #UD over when it installs (Linux: its handler replaces the backstop and re-raises with `SIG_DFL`, where today's `posix_crash.cpp` restores the backstop; Windows: a first-in-chain vectored handler sends non-trap #UD to the dump path); check 5's `ud2` and EVEX fixtures before and after crash-handler install".

02 §1.1 (docs/plan/02-engine-runtime.md:241-245), the decode rule: "It decodes the faulting opcode at `ExceptionAddress` or `si_addr`, and it handles only a genuine ISA fault: a VEX or EVEX lead byte (`C4`, `C5`, `62`, after optional `66`, `F2`, `F3` or REX prefixes), which covers every AVX, AVX2, FMA, F16C and BMI1/2 instruction, or POPCNT (`F3 0F B8`). Only those get the CPU message and exit 78."

02 §1.1:246-251, traps: `ud2` (0F 0B), `ud1` (0F B9) and `ud0` (0F FF), and every other #UD, pass straight through. Windows returns EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH. On Linux the handler returns and SA_RESETHAND has restored SIG_DFL.

02 §1.1:252-261, the takeover: "On Linux their `sigaction(SIGILL)` replaces the backstop, and their re-raise path restores `SIG_DFL`, never the saved backstop … On Windows the crash handler adds its own vectored handler first in the chain (`AddVectoredExceptionHandler(1, …)`). It sends every `STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` except the three traps to the dump path, which terminates the process, so the backstop behind it never runs again; the traps continue to SEH and the unhandled-exception filter. This keeps the gate objects at three exports. The crash report carries a `cpu_gate` annotation (the verdict, the CPU brand, the feature bits and the fault's lead bytes, classified by the same decoder from a shared `static inline` header)".

02 §1.1:262-266, the proof (audit check 5 and core_tests): "A gate test child that passes the gate executes, before the crash handler installs: `ud2`, which must die by SIGILL or an unhandled exception, never exit 78; and, under SDE `-hsw`, an EVEX (AVX-512) instruction, which must exit 78 with the message. After the crash handler installs, the same two must each produce a dump with no exit 78, the EVEX one annotated as an ISA fault."

The fixtures are WP-0.5r's. The SDE/qemu runner that executes them is WP-0.2r part 2 (09:99; 09 §5.10.4 (b) five-check-audit row).

risks: Inverting test_cpu.cpp:370's assertion (0x06 used to exit 78) looks like a weakened test to a reviewer. In the PR body and the commit, cite 02 §1.1:241-251 (round 5) and show the new, stronger assertions that replace it: VEX and EVEX give 78, other #UD gives a SIGILL death, user-sent SIGILL gives a SIGILL death.

The deterministic 'always #UD' encodings rest on SDM reserved-field rules: a non-1111b VEX.vvvv/EVEX.vvvv for instructions that do not use it. EVEX bit fields are being repurposed (AVX10.2's U bit, APX), so a future CPU could make an encoding valid. Pick fields the SDM still lists as #UD for that exact opcode, verify by execution here (an AVX-512 host), and keep the genuine AVX-512 instruction for SDE/qemu.

Genuine EVEX is host-dependent on CI. Hosted runners with AVX-512 (Xeon 8370C/8573C, EPYC 9V74) execute it, and EPYC 7763 faults. The core_tests branch on cpuGate().usable must report what it proved, and must not silently pass.

MSVC cl has no inline asm. The VirtualAlloc/VirtualProtect RX path must avoid a data-to-function-pointer cast warning (copy the pointer with memcpy) and must flush the instruction cache. It is first exercised on Windows CI, so a cl-only failure is found late.
The decoder in the gate objects must stay free of auto-vectorized loops and literal pools: cl's `__xmm@` COMDATs are unaudited in CI. Write it straight-line.

The Linux signal-handler annotation must stay async-signal-safe. Precompute the brand and features at install, because cpuGate() allocates std::string. Read lead bytes lazily, only bytes the CPU fetched, so the handler never takes a SIGSEGV of its own.

The Windows VEH(1) also sees first-chance #UD inside __try blocks. No vendored code probes x86 instructions that way today (grep of third_party), but a future dependency could, and the takeover would dump and kill it. Record this in crash.h.

In HELIOS_PROFILE builds Tracy replaces the SIGILL disposition (Linux) and the UEF (Windows) when a profiler connects (TracyProfiler.cpp:1611-1634, :2043, TRACY_ON_DEMAND). The backstop and takeover guarantees do not hold while a Tracy client is connected. This predates part 2 and is out of scope; mention it in the README.
